direction: January moves through three kinds of contact with water: first rain on dry earth, a river reduced to a bottle, and a lotus rising from dark water. Close material study, a spare object-and-river composition and a low pond view give distinct emotional and visual scales. Ecological testimony, equity and the difficult turns of self-doubt remain text-led.

items.title: First rain on dry earth
items.rationale: An unexpected meeting moistens the speaker’s dry inner sky. Close rain touching earth suggests that first inward change without inventing the two people or assembling the poem’s lightning, ice and stars.

review.notes: PASS: absorbing wet marks merge irregularly into a small damp area while dry earth retains quiet space. Cropped shoot stays secondary; no theatrical storm or decorative cracked-desert pattern. Watercolor granulation and selective graphite remain materially coherent. The tentative first contact suits the poem’s unexpected meeting without invented people. independent:false.

items.alt: Fresh rain darkens patches of dry earth beside a small cropped green shoot.

items.title: The river held in a bottle
items.rationale: The ode contrasts the river’s indifferent continuity with sacred water enclosed and sold. One ordinary bottle beside a broad river wash suggests that tension without reconstructing Kashi, funeral rites or monuments.

review.notes: PASS: modest unlabelled bottle against the moving river holds the poem’s tension between enclosure and continuity. Water level is horizontal, glass/stone distortion and contact shadow plausible. Light is stronger than prompt but coherent from right, no artificial aura or commercial product shine. Gouache character retained, no monument, rite or location accuracy claim. independent:false.

items.alt: A small unlabelled bottle of water stands on a stone step beside a moving river.

items.title: Above the dark water
items.rationale: The poem locates freedom in a lotus emerging from dark water. A sideward flower partly withheld by its leaf keeps that awakening grounded rather than a centered sacred emblem.

review.notes: PASS: side-on lotus has uneven overlapping petals and a partly withheld center; cropped cupped leaf and broken reflection place growth in real dark water. Stem meets water plausibly, no symmetrical emblem, jewels, aura or sacred portrait. Brushed pastel/watercolor remains distinct from the two pale January studies. independent:false.

items.alt: A pale pink lotus rises beside a cupped green leaf above dark water.

text_led.rationale: The poem names a lost riverbank community and its transformation; preserve its testimony without fabricating a documentary reconstruction or deity.
The direct argument for equity at home is strongest as an open address; avoid symbolic gender stereotypes.
The sharp shifts among self-doubt, a remembered death, detergent and anxiety should stay in the language; avoid depicting the named woman or reducing the poem to household props.
